title: Whole subject-of-faith dispute is philosophical, not piety
source_text: XXX. Caeterum hic observandum est totam hanc Disputationem de Fidei Subjecto, uti plures alias, esse Philosophicam, & nihil ad pietatem & Religionem attinere. Nam ad hanc quidem maxime pertinet, ut sciamus quid nobis agendum & faciendum sit, ut Christi Domini nostri mandata obsequamur de Evangelio vera vivaque fide amplectendo: An autem actus illi quibus constat vera fides sint mentis vel voluntatis, ad pietatem nihil omnino facit, non magis quam illa quaestio, An mens & voluntas sint duae facultates realiter distinctae, an vero una eademque diversimode solum considerata? Item, quod hodie quoque vocatur in controversiam, An judicium sit actus mentis, an voluntatis? Quae Philosophis possunt per otium discutienda & examinanda relinqui.
pass_a_gloss: But here it is to be observed that this whole Disputation on Faith's Subject, like several others, is philosophical and pertains nothing to piety and Religion. For to religion it especially belongs that we know what we must do and perform, that we obey our Lord Christ's commands about embracing the Gospel with true and living faith: but whether those acts of which true faith consists are of mind or of will makes nothing at all for piety — no more than the question whether mind and will are two faculties really distinct, or one and the same only considered diversely; likewise what is today also called into controversy, whether judgment is an act of mind or of will. Which things can be left to philosophers to discuss and examine at leisure.
pass_b_english: Le Blanc: the subject-of-faith fight is philosophical, not piety.
Piety needs living embrace of the Gospel; mind-vs-will faculty questions can wait for philosophers.

choices.why: Scholastic faculty debate, not gospel duty.
